evidenceType: Actual registered subject types and drafted learning outcomes
limitations: The counts are templates, not vetted unique lessons, independently validated skills or curriculum standards. Small banks are marked underrepresented. Project submissions are not automatically graded.

goals: Explain observations using words or pictures
Identify basic shapes, patterns, and story meaning

appliedAssignment.title: Explain a pattern
appliedAssignment.prompt: Find a simple pattern in shapes, sounds or numbers. Describe or dictate what repeats. Draw it on paper and describe what comes next.
rubric: Explains why the next item follows

goals: Add, subtract and reason with place value
Read and explain a short passage

appliedAssignment.title: Measure and describe
appliedAssignment.prompt: Choose three objects, predict which is longest, measure or compare them safely, then write or dictate how your prediction compared with the result.

goals: Work with two-digit operations, fractions and measurements

appliedAssignment.title: A question from everyday life
appliedAssignment.prompt: Ask a measurable question, collect five observations or counts, summarize the findings and explain one limitation of your method.
rubric: Describes the evidence and a limitation

appliedAssignment.title: Explain an investigation
appliedAssignment.prompt: Compare two plausible explanations for an observation in nature. Identify what evidence would distinguish them and write a connected paragraph.

goals: Reason with fractions, area and multi-step problems
Describe scientific evidence and community decisions

appliedAssignment.title: A community and environment study
appliedAssignment.prompt: Choose an issue affecting your community or local environment. Research two distinct sources, describe a measurable feature and propose a fair way to test one improvement.

goals: Solve decimal, fraction and measurement problems

appliedAssignment.title: A quantitative decision
appliedAssignment.prompt: Collect or find data about a real decision, use fractions or decimals to compare options, show your calculations and defend a conclusion including uncertainty.

goals: Analyze ratios, negative numbers and basic statistics
Explain systems in science and history

appliedAssignment.title: Evaluate an evidence claim
appliedAssignment.prompt: Select a claim from science, history or economics. Find independent evidence for and against it, calculate a relevant ratio or rate, and explain what evidence would change your conclusion.
rubric: States a falsifiable or contestable claim
Uses at least two independent sources
Computes and explains a quantitative comparison

appliedAssignment.title: Model a system
appliedAssignment.prompt: Choose a real-world process. Represent two related variables in an equation, chart or table; test whether the model predicts observations; identify assumptions and weaknesses.

goals: Assess source reliability and statistical claims

appliedAssignment.title: Compare competing arguments
appliedAssignment.prompt: Take a question in literature, science or public policy. Present the strongest argument on each side, assess at least three pieces of evidence and propose a justified position.

goals: Use computational reasoning and documented methods

appliedAssignment.title: Reproducible inquiry
appliedAssignment.prompt: Design and document a small investigation. State a testable hypothesis, explain sampling, build a data table, discuss bias and show how somebody could reproduce the results.

goals: Analyze quadratics, probability and experimental error
Evaluate causal claims and complex evidence

appliedAssignment.title: Causal and statistical reasoning
appliedAssignment.prompt: Analyze a dataset that seems to support a causal claim. Describe the variables, alternative explanations, statistics, uncertainty, limitations and a more credible follow-up design.

goals: Use advanced algebra, chemistry and physics models
Interpret primary sources and quantitative studies

appliedAssignment.title: Cross-disciplinary research argument
appliedAssignment.prompt: Investigate a question requiring at least two school subjects. Review at least four credible sources, articulate an original argument, test a competing explanation and disclose your methods.

goals: Integrate calculus, statistics and scientific reasoning
Write and defend rigorous cross-disciplinary analyses
Independently investigate unfamiliar problems and limitations

appliedAssignment.title: Grade 12 independent capstone
appliedAssignment.prompt: Investigate an original, advanced research or engineering problem. Define specifications or a research question; cite appropriate sources; provide calculations, tests or analyses; discuss negative results and competing explanations; include reproducibility and a substantial written conclusion.
